chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Alawi, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the marriage of women who have been divorced three times, so he said to me, 'Indeed, your divorce is not permissible for others, and their divorce is permissible for you, because you do not consider the three divorces to be anything (i.e., not final).'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on a woman divorced three times remarrying her first husband?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) elucidates the Shia doctrine of *Tafwid* (delegation) in divorce, where the husband retains the right to revoke the finality of three divorces unless he explicitly delegates this authority to the wife. The Imam grounds this ruling in the practical reality that men typically do not consider the third divorce to be truly final or binding in the same absolute sense as the first two, thereby allowing the original couple to remarry without the need for *Nikah al-Mu'abbad* (intermediary marriage). This contrasts with the Sunni view which generally treats the third divorce as an irrevocable barrier requiring a new marriage to a third party before remarriage is possible.
